author: Claude
subject: Timetable Generator: windowed scheduling, observed holidays, editable timetable
body:
Faithful rewrite per the amendment — the engine moves from month-anchored
auto-distribution to explicit per-module date windows.

1. Observed public holidays: a Singapore public holiday on a Sunday auto-blocks
   the following Monday ("<name> observed"). blockedDates now unions UCC +
   public + observed; nothing schedules on weekends or any blocked day. The
   preview shows an "Automatically observed" note.
2. Module Start/End Date: each module carries its own scheduling window (fields
   below Classroom). generateCourseSchedule places lessons on the EARLIEST valid
   teaching days within each module's window; lessons never fall outside it or
   on a blocked day.
3. Fit validation: validateModuleFit warns (non-blocking) when a module's
   available teaching days are fewer than its lessons, or a window is missing;
   only the days that fit are scheduled.
4. Conflict rule: a clash is flagged ONLY when two different modules share the
   same teacher AND overlapping time AND the same classroom on a date (class
   group no longer triggers it). Applies to generated and amended entries.
5. Manual amendment: a new "Amend" view makes every generated entry editable
   (date, times, teacher, classroom, module, lesson, activity); edits update the
   timetable immediately and re-run conflict detection.
6. Duplicate module: copies all fields into a new, independently-editable row.

Retired the now-incompatible month-anchored distribution, AL buffer days, and
the module-shift panel (manual editing supersedes shift); List/Calendar/Hybrid
views and exports keep working over the generated lessons. Start month and
delivery mode inputs removed from the form (kept on the type for imports).

Engine + validation tests rewritten; 170 tests pass. Browser sweep 13/13
(windowed generation, observed-Monday skipped, fit warnings, all-three conflict
matrix via manual amend, Duplicate). tsc, vite build, oxlint clean.

author: Claude
subject: Review planner: add Delivery Mode (Series +1mo / Parallel +3mo)
body:
Amendment to Module & Course Review:
- ModuleReview gains a deliveryMode ('Series' | 'Parallel'); a dropdown column
  renders on every Module Review row.
- Module Review Date = Actual Start + 1 month (Series) or + 3 months
  (Parallel), month-end safe; recomputes live on Actual Start or Delivery Mode
  change.
- Course roll-ups are unchanged in logic — Per Cycle still takes the latest
  Module Review Date among matching modules, which now respects each module's
  delivery mode (verified against the amendment's Eng example: latest = the
  Parallel modules' +3mo date).

Sorting, validation, roll-up fallback, and persistence all unchanged. 4 new
unit tests (179 total). Browser sweep 9/9. tsc, oxlint clean.

author: Claude
subject: Add "Cult of the Lamb" theme (4th skin)
body:
Dark gothic-cult skin, added purely via the token system + registry — no new
code path, no layout change, tracker logic/exports untouched.

- New :root[data-theme='cult-of-the-lamb'] variable set (pins its palette,
  ignores light/dark). Crimson is a FILL (buttons, headers, table headers);
  accent TEXT/icons resolve to muted gold; form fields are a light parchment
  surface with charcoal text while buttons/cards stay dark. Active tab/nav uses
  cult purple (#4B2E4D), distinct from the crimson primary-action fill. Serif
  headings via a system font (no CDN); a subtle page-only vignette.
- Status/badge roles mapped so every existing chip/banner/auto-note picks them
  up: success = near-black on gold, warning = white on blood orange, danger =
  white on crimson, neutral = charcoal, planner fills stay light with dark ink.
- Registered in theme.ts (Skin, SKINS, isSkin) and the index.html pre-paint
  validator; default stays Y2K Pop.
- Small Cult-only decorative treatment on Home tiles + empty states (gold rings,
  a crescent) — kept out of tables and inputs.

Contrast: all pairings pass WCAG AA (verified in-browser) — bone/near-black
14.6, bone/charcoal 12.6, charcoal/parchment 9.7, white/blood-orange 5.06 (bone
was 4.07 so warning text nudged to white — text-only, brand hex untouched),
bone/crimson 7.3, near-black/gold 7.6. Browser sweep 19/19 incl. live-apply,
persistence, and no regression to the other three skins. 175 tests pass; tsc,
vite build, oxlint clean.

author: Claude
subject: Theme tokens: split fill/text accent, field surface, and active state
body:
Prepare for a dark skin whose accent works as a fill but not as text, and
whose input fields are a light surface while buttons stay dark. All new tokens
default to existing values, so Classic / Retro LCD / Y2K Pop are unchanged.

- --field-bg / --field-ink: form-field surface + its text, separate from
  --input-bg (shared by buttons/chips/cards). Rerouted the input/select/
  textarea/.rv-input rules to these.
- --accent-text: accent used as TEXT/ICON colour (rerouted the color: usages
  of --accent — links, demo button, brand icon, module legend, the
  "auto-calculated" note — leaving fills/borders on --accent).
- --active / --active-ring: active tab/nav indicator, rerouted the segmented,
  stepper, month-chip, and sidebar-active selectors so a skin can make active
  state a distinct hue from the primary-action fill.
- --border-strong: emphasised border variant.

tsc, oxlint clean; 175 tests pass.

author: Claude
subject: Consolidate Module & Course Review: roll-up starts + sortable table
body:
Keep the single workspace-hub Review planner (shared tokens/theme) and port
the behaviour that was missing versus the standalone draft, adapting it to the
existing component — no Tailwind, no second component/route (there was no
separate file to delete; the registry already exposes one route).

Logic ported in (src/tools/review-planner/reviewModel.ts):
- courseRollupStart: Course Planned/Actual Start now roll up to the EARLIEST
  start among modules whose course name matches (trim + case-insensitive, the
  same normalisation as Per Cycle). With no matching modules they fall back to
  manual entry, exactly like Per Cycle. computeCourse now returns all four
  course dates.
- sortModuleRows: Module Review table sorts by Course/Module name (case-
  insensitive) or Planned/Actual start (chronological, parsed as local dates),
  ascending then toggling to descending on repeat click; empty values always
  sink to the end. Sorting is a display-only copy, so stored order and row
  identity (edit/delete by id) are untouched.

UI (ReviewPlannerPage.tsx):
- Clickable sort headers with a direction arrow.
- Course Planned/Actual/Per Cycle show ONE formatted DD MMMM YYYY value with an
  "auto-calculated" note when modules match, and an editable date input when
  they don't. Removed the old raw-date-input-plus-caption pattern: editable
  dates are a single native control; computed dates are a single formatted
  value — never both.

11 new unit tests (175 total). Browser sweep 15/15: roll-ups (earliest start,
auto note, manual fallback), sorting (toggle, chronological, empty-last,
edit-while-sorted by id), single-value dates, validation, delete, persistence.
tsc, vite build, oxlint clean.

author: Claude
subject: Theme step 2: three skins + data-theme switch + no-flash load
body:
- Define Classic / Retro LCD / Y2K Pop as CSS custom-property sets scoped by
  :root[data-theme=...]. Classic is the base :root (+ data-mode dark). Retro
  LCD (olive-green duotone, condensed all-caps labels, LCD scan-line page
  texture) and Y2K Pop (pink/teal/cream, heavy black outlines, hard offset
  shadows, playful heading font) PIN their own palettes and ignore light/dark
  (documented in each block). Table headers get their own --th-bg/--th-ink so
  data cells stay high-contrast in every skin.
- ThemeProvider is the single source of truth: it stamps data-theme on <html>
  and persists the choice under "ucc:workspace:theme". Default skin is Y2K Pop
  (a code comment notes Classic reads best for dense tables).
- index.html pre-paint now stamps BOTH data-mode and data-theme before first
  paint, so there is no flash of the wrong theme. Google Fonts (Oswald,
  Fredoka) load with system fallbacks — headings degrade gracefully if the CDN
  is unreachable; data never depends on a web font.

tsc, vite build, oxlint clean.

author: Claude
subject: Theme step 1: tokenise colours/fonts and split colour-mode onto data-mode
body:
Prepare for skinnable themes without changing the current look:

- Add themeable CSS variables to :root: --on-accent, --th-bg/--th-ink (table
  header, so each skin can guarantee cell-header contrast), --radius/-lg/-pill,
  --card-border-width, --card-shadow(/-hover), --font-body/--font-heading,
  --label-transform/--label-spacing, and --page-texture.
- Components now read those tokens (replaced hardcoded #fff → var(--on-accent),
  panel/card/button radius + shadow, table-header colours, label casing).
- Split the two theming axes onto separate root attributes so they compose:
  colour scheme moves from data-theme to **data-mode** (light|dark), freeing
  **data-theme** to carry the skin next. index.html pre-paint and
  SettingsProvider now stamp data-mode; the dark palette keys off
  :root[data-mode='dark'].

Pure refactor — Classic light/dark render identically. tsc, oxlint clean;
164 tests pass.

subject: Add the Module & Course Review planner tool and register it
body:
Second workspace tracker, self-contained under src/tools/review-planner/

validation (164 total). Browser sweep 19/19: registry-driven Home + sidebar,

subject: Add an ERPNext field-mapping screen; lesson names stay manual
body:
Replaces the hardcoded ERPNEXT_FIELD_MAP with a per-DocType mapping
the user builds in Settings, since every ERPNext deployment names its
fields differently.

- src/erpFieldMapping.ts: the fixed set of app target fields (course
  name, teacher, classroom, Module Class Details, total lessons, start
  date/time, end time, optional activity — lesson names are NOT a
  target, they stay manually typed) and per-DocType localStorage
  persistence for the mapping.
- src/erpnext.ts: fetchSampleFields() lists one record of the DocType
  then fetches its full doc (through the existing /erp proxy) and
  returns its top-level scalar field names, excluding child
  tables/links. mapDocToForm/listErpRecords/fetchErpRecord now take
  the saved mapping instead of a hardcoded map; the fields query for
  the picker is built from only the mapped source keys.
- Settings: "Load sample fields" button + a mapping table (ERPNext
  field dropdown -> fixed app field), inline guidance gated by the
  existing Help toggle, and a note that lesson names are manual.
- Import: with the saved mapping, a DocType with exactly one record
  imports it directly with a note instead of showing a picker;
  unmapped targets stay blank; lesson names are never overwritten.
- No key or secret in any URL — mapped fields, not credentials, appear
  in query strings; all calls stay on /erp in dev.
- 12 new tests (fetchSampleFields scalar filtering + errors, mapping
  storage round-trip/per-DocType, mapDocToForm/listErpRecords/
  fetchErpRecord against the mapping): 143 passing.

author: Claude
subject: Route ERPNext through the Vite dev proxy to fix CORS
body:
The ERPNext server returns no CORS headers for the Codespace origin, so
direct browser fetches died with a bare "Failed to fetch" even though
the key/secret were valid (curl worked — no CORS outside the browser).

- vite.config.ts: '/erp' proxy → https://sms.unitedceres.edu.sg
  (changeOrigin, secure, prefix rewrite). Target is static at config
  time; the dev server must be restarted after editing it.
  ERP_PROXY_TARGET env override exists so tests can aim it at a mock.
- src/erpnext.ts: new erpBase() — '/erp' in dev, the configured base
  URL (trailing slash trimmed) in production builds. The connection
  test, record list, and single-doc fetch all build URLs from it.
- Clear failures: 401/403 now reads "Authentication failed (…) — check
  the API key, secret, and role permissions"; a thrown fetch reads as a
  network/CORS-preflight failure instead of only "Failed to fetch".
- Credentials stay in the Authorization header only — never in a URL or
  query string (asserted in tests).
- Settings: hint under Base URL explaining the dev proxy; README CORS
  note rewritten.
- 7 new tests (erpBase dev/prod, success/401/network messages, URL has
  no secret): 131 passing.

author: Claude
subject: v5 step 5: module shift with end-of-month deadline guard
body:
- shiftModuleLater(lessons, moduleId, 1|2, holidays): every lesson in the
  module advances the chosen number of VALID teaching days (weekends and
  holidays are skipped as steps), order and lesson numbering preserved. The
  module's window months are fixed; in series mode its AL fill is rebuilt so
  vacated days become AL and consumed buffer days become lessons.
- Deadline guard: the module's last lesson must stay on or before the last
  valid teaching day of its final window month. A breaching shift is rejected
  with a warning naming the module and the deadline (DD MMMM YYYY), leaving
  the schedule untouched.
- Modules panel above the conflicts panel: per-module lesson count and span
  plus "Shift +1 day" / "+2 days" controls; conflicts re-scan after every
  applied shift.
- Series spread switched from the end-anchored round formula to an anchored
  floor stride (i*n/take): spacing stays roughly equal but the final lesson no
  longer sits ON the month's last valid day, leaving the trailing AL slack the
  shift feature consumes — with the old formula every series shift would have
  hit the deadline immediately and the feature could never apply.

6 shift tests (AL consumption + window coverage, holiday-skipping steps,
deadline block naming the date, repeated shifts until blocked, parallel
blocks, other modules untouched) — suite 120 passing. Browser-verified:
+1 shift moves 01→02 July with success banner and re-scan, repeated +2
shifts end in the deadline warning.

author: Claude
subject: v5 step 4: cross-module conflict detection, highlighting, and panel
body:
- detectConflicts scans all real lessons (AL excluded) pairwise per date:
  same teacher, classroom, or class group claimed by DIFFERENT modules at
  overlapping time ranges (startA < endB && startB < endA) produces a typed
  Conflict { type, date, moduleIds, detail } naming both modules and ranges.
  A copy of the lesson list comes back with conflicts attached to every
  affected lesson.
- Generation runs the scan automatically; conflicts live in the
  route-persistent store.
- Highlighting in all three views: List rows tinted with a warning icon and
  detail tooltip, Calendar chips turn warning-coloured with the icon, Hybrid
  activity cells get a conflict fill that beats the kind colour (the planner
  Sheets/CSV exports inherit the same conflict fill).
- Conflicts panel above the views: each clash as DD MMMM YYYY, clash type,
  the two modules with their time ranges; a green all-clear renders when a
  generated course has no clashes.

6 engine tests (per-day classroom clashes, independent teacher/class-group
flags, non-overlap negative, series-clean, per-lesson attachment, AL
exclusion) — suite 114. Browser-verified: series demo all-clear with AL,
parallel demo raises classroom + class-group clashes highlighted in every
view.

author: Claude
subject: v5 step 2: month-anchored starts, series/parallel distribution, AL fill
body:
Replace the step-1 first-cut placement with the real engine:

- firstTeachingDayOfMonth / validTeachingDaysOfMonth: a module begins on the
  1st of its month, or the next valid teaching day when the 1st is a weekend
  or UCC/public holiday.
- Series: each active month takes min(remaining, valid days) lessons spread
  evenly across the month's valid teaching days (even-interval selection);
  every remaining valid weekday in an active month becomes an AL buffer entry
  (kind "AL", no teacher, no room, label from the AL_LABEL constant).
  Overflow continues on the following month's first teaching day.
- Parallel: lessons cluster onto contiguous valid teaching days from the
  month's first teaching day, crossing months as needed; no AL fill.
- generateCourseSchedule sequences series modules (module N+1 starts the month
  after module N's final lesson month) and starts parallel modules together
  at the course start month.

15 engine tests: anchored starts (weekend/holiday 1sts), spread + AL fill,
full-month overflow, numbering/activity cycling, contiguous parallel blocks
across month boundaries, series sequencing, holiday exclusion. Suite: 104.

subject: Implement multi-group scheduling and clash detection
body:
Replace the v1 stubs with working engine pieces (no UI surface yet — the
multi-group dashboard remains a future pass):

- generateMultiGroupSchedule: schedules each group against the shared holiday
  calendar and merges, ordered by date / start time / group. Per-group
  one-session-per-day is preserved; cross-group conflicts are deliberately
  left in the data for detectClashes to surface rather than silently
  reshuffled.
- detectClashes(lessons, holidays?): duplicateSession (a group scheduled
  twice on a date), teacher / classroom / classGroup (the same resource
  claimed by two or more different groups at overlapping times), and
  uccHoliday / publicHoliday (lessons on holiday dates — reachable via
  imported or hand-merged data) when a HolidaySet is provided. One Clash per
  (type, date, resource), carrying every involved lesson and the holiday
  name where known.

11 new tests: merge counts and ordering, per-group parity with the
single-group scheduler, each clash type, the non-overlap and empty-resource
negative cases, and named-holiday details. Suite: 89 passing.

subject: Preserve timetable and wizard state across route changes
body:
React Router unmounts the Timetable page when the user visits /settings, so
the generated timetable, chosen view, and wizard progress were silently
discarded on every round trip.

- Add TimetableProvider above the routes holding the wizard state, wizard
  step, layout choice, generated lessons/config/holidays, active view, and

  also fixes "Back to wizard" resetting to Step 1 after a layout toggle.
- Replace the per-caller useSettings hook with a SettingsProvider + context:
  one shared state instance, so same-tab updates propagate live (the storage
  event never fires in the document that wrote it — the old design only
  looked correct because remounts re-read localStorage). Cross-tab sync via
  the storage event stays in the provider.

summary, and wizard step all survive a /settings round trip; settings changes
propagate without a reload. Vitest suite still 70/70.

author: Claude
subject: Fix three correctness issues from code review
body:
1. Activities pair to lesson names by index, but parseLines dropped blank
   lines, silently shifting every later activity onto the wrong lesson. Add
   parseAlignedLines (preserves interior blanks, trims trailing ones) and use
   it for activities only.
2. Holiday and start dates were shape-checked (YYYY-MM-DD) but not
   calendar-checked, so 2026-02-30 rolled over to 02 March and suppressed the
   wrong teaching day. Add isValidIsoDate (round-trip parse/format) and apply
   it in validateRules and to startDate (reachable via ERPNext import).
3. The Google Sheets exports called window.open only after the OAuth + API
   awaits, outside the click gesture, so popup blockers could eat the tab and
   the created sheet never opened. openTabForAsyncUrl opens a placeholder tab
   synchronously and navigates or closes it when the URL resolves.

author: Claude
subject: Add UCC School Timetable Generator (React + TS + Vite)
body:
Client-only SPA that generates an evenly-spread teaching timetable for a
class group and exports it to CSV and PDF.

- Timezone-safe local date handling (no toISOString for YYYY-MM-DD) so
  Singapore UTC+8 dates never shift back a day.
- Two scheduling modes: every valid weekday, and even per-month spread via
  interval selection (throws with month + counts when a month can't fit).
- Multi-group data model and detectClashes/generateMultiGroupSchedule typed
  stubs so future passes slot in without refactoring.
- Per-rule form validation, nine-column preview + summary strip.
- CSV (native Blob) and PDF (jsPDF landscape via jspdf-autotable, functional
  autoTable(doc, ...) form) exports.
- Vite dev server bound to host:true port 5173 for Codespace port forwarding.

Excel export is stubbed and its button disabled: the required SheetJS 0.20.3
CDN tarball is blocked by the environment network policy and the stale public
npm xlsx build was ruled out.
